The portion of the upper human appendage, from the shoulder to the wrist and sometimes including the hand.

examples.text: She stood with her right arm extended and her palm forward to indicate “Stop!”

glosses: The extended portion of the upper limb, from the shoulder to the elbow.

examples.text: The arm and forearm are parts of the upper limb in the human body.

glosses: A limb, or locomotive or prehensile organ, of an invertebrate animal.

examples.text: the arms of an octopus

glosses: The part of a piece of clothing that covers the arm.

examples.text: […] one arm of this jacket streamed behind him like the broidered arm of a huzzar’s surcoat.
[…] he noticed that a dark stain had appeared under the arm of her grey silk dress.
Samad made a grab for the boy and caught him by the arm of his shirt.

glosses: A long, narrow, more or less rigid part of an object extending from the main part or centre of the object, such as the armrest of an armchair, a crane, a pair of spectacles or a pair of compasses.

examples.text: The robot arm reached out and placed the part on the assembly line.

glosses: A bay or inlet off a main body of water.

examples.text: Shelburne Bay is an arm of Lake Champlain.

glosses: A branch of an organization.

examples.text: the cavalry arm of the military service
Congress has asked the Government Accountability Office, its investigative arm, to review the workplace complaints raised by air marshals, said Charles Young, a spokesman for the office.

glosses: Power; might; strength; support.

examples.text: the arm of the law

glosses: A pitcher

examples.text: The team needs to sign another arm in the offseason.

glosses: One of the two parts of a chromosome.

examples.text: And make him with our pikes and partisans / A grave: come, arm him.

glosses: Poor; lacking in riches or wealth.

examples.text: The Duke's arms were a sable gryphon rampant on an argent field.

To supply with armour or (later especially) weapons.

examples.text: The king armed his knights with swords and shields.

They were arming them with spears and shields, putting iron halfhelms on their heads, and arraying them along the inner wall, a rank of snowy sentinels. "Lord Winter has joined us with his levies," one of the sentries [said].

glosses: To supply with the equipment, knowledge, authority, or other tools needed for a particular task; to furnish with capability; to equip.

glosses: To prepare (a tool, weapon, or system) for action; to activate.

examples.text: Remember to arm the alarm system before leaving for work.

glosses: To become prepared for action; to activate.

examples.text: Torpedoes were loosed, but the range was too short for them to actually arm, and they bounced harmlessly off the ship as it cut loose with its secondary and antiaircraft guns, smashing anything that it could see.

glosses: To cover or furnish with a plate, or with whatever will add strength, force, security, or efficiency.

examples.text: to arm the hilt of a sword; to arm a hook in angling

glosses: To take up weapons; to arm oneself.
